Hi all, I have some trouble using to_dual. I am trying to dualize HomologyPretheory. Below is a minimal example that exhibits the problem. In this example, I am trying to dualize Foo. I wrote a new structure Cofoo for the dual and annotated it with to_dual existing. This worked fine. However, when I want to transport results about Foo to Cofoo automatically (e.g. Foo.rfl), it complains that it expects Cofoo.F to have type C ⥤ D (but it has type Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D). If I understand correctly, it does not translate C ⥤ D to Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D since C is a constant.

I tried explicitly annotating Cofoo.F with to_dual to make it understand that it is supposed to be dual to Foo.F but it throws the same error there. (Also, this confuses me a bit since when annotating Cofoo with to_dual? existing, it tells me it is already translating Cofoo.F to Foo.F.) Upon a suggestion by @Edward van de Meent, I also tried splitting Foo.F into separate fields for its components (obj, map, etc.) but this results in a similar type mismatch between X ⟶ Y and Y ⟶ X.

Does anybody have another idea how to make this work? Thanks!

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory

variable (C D : Type*) [Category* C] [Category* D]

structure Foo where
  F : C ⥤ D

@[to_dual? existing Foo]
structure Cofoo where
  F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D

attribute [to_dual existing] Cofoo.F

@[to_dual]
protected lemma Foo.rfl (X : Foo C D) : X.F = X.F := rfl

The strategy of to_dual at its core is to replace constants with their duals, and to reorder arguments when necessary. So, it will never 'magically' insert or remove a ᵒᵖ in the expression.

Note that I have a PR in progress (#40365) that makes to_dual validate annotations on structure more carefully, so after that PR, your to_dual annotation on Cofoo will give you a warning.

Note also that the dual of C ⥤ D is just C ⥤ D itself, assuming that you dualize in both C and D. to_dual currently does not support dualizing only one of C and D in C ⥤ D.

the strange thing is that unbundeling inlining doesn't work here; if you make separate structures for co- and contravariant functors and point to_dual from one to the other, it fails to properly dualise them

Yes. The problem is that to dualize C ⥤ D, to_dual needs to determine whether C should be dualized, and whether D should be dualized, and based on that, decide whether the funtor turns into a contravariant functor (namely if exactly one of the two gets dualized). Currently, we only have a yes/no decision for whether to translate a constant, and we have a unique translation for in the yes case. The same problem comes up with Monotone and Antitone.
(This is a feature that I'd like to have, but I don't have short term plans for implementing it.)

to my surprise, the following works, showing that it is not completely unattainable to have to_dual dualize "functors" in a way that fixes the domain:

Code

import Mathlib

namespace CategoryTheory

structure Presheaf (C D : Type*) [Category* C] [Category* D] where
  obj : C → D
  map {X Y : C} : (X ⟶ Y) → (obj Y ⟶ obj X)
  map_id (X : C) : map (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (obj X) := by cat_disch
  map_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = map g ≫ map f := by cat_disch


@[to_dual existing (relevant_arg := 2) Presheaf]
structure CoPresheaf (C D : Type*) [Category* C] [Category* D] where
  obj : C → D
  map {X Y : C} : (X ⟶ Y) → (obj X ⟶ obj Y)
  map_id (X : C) : map (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (obj X) := by cat_disch
  map_comp {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = map f ≫ map g := by cat_disch

@[to_dual]
def Presheaf.parallelPair {C : Type*} [Category* C] {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : Presheaf (Limits.WalkingParallelPair) C where
  obj := fun
  | .zero => Y
  | .one => X
  map := fun
  | .left => f
  | .right => g
  | .id .zero => 𝟙 Y
  | .id .one => 𝟙 X
  map_comp {X' Y' Z'} h₁ h₂ := by
    symm
    match X',Y',Z', h₁, h₂ with
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .id .zero => exact Category.comp_id (𝟙 Y)
    | _,_,_,.id .one, .id .one => exact (Category.comp_id (𝟙 X))
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .left => exact Category.comp_id _
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .right => exact Category.comp_id _
    | _,_,_,.left, .id .one => exact Category.id_comp _
    | _,_,_,.right, .id .one => exact Category.id_comp _

@[to_dual]
def CoPresheaf.parallelPair' {C : Type*} [Category* C] {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : CoPresheaf (Limits.WalkingParallelPair) C where
  obj := fun
  | .zero => X
  | .one => Y
  map := fun
  | .left => f
  | .right => g
  | .id .zero => 𝟙 X
  | .id .one => 𝟙 Y
  map_comp {X' Y' Z'} h₁ h₂ := by
    symm
    match X',Y',Z', h₁, h₂ with
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .id .zero => exact Category.comp_id _
    | _,_,_,.id .one, .id .one => exact Category.comp_id _
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .left => exact Category.id_comp _
    | _,_,_,.id .zero, .right => exact Category.id_comp _
    | _,_,_,.left, .id .one => exact Category.comp_id _
    | _,_,_,.right, .id .one => exact Category.comp_id _

#check Presheaf.parallelPair' -- succeeds
#check CoPresheaf.parallelPair -- succeeds as well

(i wrote both definitions by hand to see if to_dual actually properly translates the names, since to_dual? on CoPresheaf seems to indicate that it wouldn't properly translate "Presheaf" to "CoPresheaf"

This gave me the idea to simply make abbrevs for (Co)Presheaf and dualize them. This solves the error in my initial example but now I get an error when I want to_dual to generate the dual of a Category instance on Foo (see below). It seems like it unfolds the abbrev here before checking if it has a dual. Might there be a way to let it first check for a dual?

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory

variable (C D : Type*) [Category* C] [Category* D]

abbrev Presheaf := Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D

@[to_dual existing Presheaf]
abbrev CoPresheaf := C ⥤ D

structure Foo where
  F : CoPresheaf C D

structure Foo.Hom (X Y : Foo C D) where
  hom : X.F ⟶ Y.F

@[to_dual existing Foo]
structure Cofoo where
  F : Presheaf C D

@[to_dual existing]
structure Cofoo.Hom (X Y : Cofoo C D) where
  hom : X.F ⟶ Y.F

@[to_dual]
protected lemma Foo.rfl (X : Foo C D) : X.F = X.F := rfl

@[to_dual instCategoryCofoo] -- this fails with a type-mismatch between `Category (C ⥤ D)` and `Category (Presheaf C D)
instance : Category (Foo C D) where
  Hom := Foo.Hom C D
  id _ := ⟨𝟙 _⟩
  comp f g := ⟨f.hom ≫ g.hom⟩
i think the issue is that to_dual can't handle Opposite, so it fails to properly dualise CoPresheaf to Presheaf?
you mean even when creating the abbrevs it is not properly dualizing them?
i think so yes
Because it does seem to work in Foo.rfl.
sure, but the proof of that lemma doesn't become any different when you dualise
the issue happens when you try to use map on something that isn't an endomorphism

I'm not sure that is the problem here. If I dualize also the category structures on (Co)Presheaf, this error goes away. But then it seems to not properly dualize (Co)Foo.Hom.hom because it gives type mismatches between X.F ⟶ Y.F and Y.F ⟶ X.F. Can we somehow use to_dual_dont_translate to tell it not to translate those two?

Code

import Mathlib

open CategoryTheory

variable (C D : Type*) [Category* C] [Category* D]

abbrev Presheaf := Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D

instance : Category (Presheaf C D) := inferInstance

@[to_dual existing Presheaf]
abbrev CoPresheaf := C ⥤ D

@[to_dual existing instCategoryPresheaf]
instance : Category (CoPresheaf C D) := inferInstance

structure Foo where
  F : CoPresheaf C D

structure Foo.Hom (X Y : Foo C D) where
  hom : X.F ⟶ Y.F

@[to_dual existing Foo]
structure Cofoo where
  F : Presheaf C D

@[to_dual existing]
structure Cofoo.Hom (X Y : Cofoo C D) where
  hom : X.F ⟶ Y.F

attribute [to_dual existing] Cofoo.Hom.hom

@[to_dual]
protected lemma Foo.rfl (X : Foo C D) : X.F = X.F := rfl

@[to_dual instCategoryCofoo]
instance : Category (Foo C D) where
  Hom := Foo.Hom C D
  id _ := ⟨𝟙 _⟩
  comp f g := ⟨f.hom ≫ g.hom⟩
you can tell it to permute the X and Y arguments i think?

The structure approach is more robust than the abbrev approach, because to_dual assumes that the dual a def/abbrev is the same as the dual of the value. This however doesn't change the fact that to_dual cannot add or remove the opposite in the expression.
